newsitem.title: POLAND: BWR, SECESYJNY TO DECIDE ON MERGER IN DEC.
newsitem.headline: BWR, SECESYJNY TO DECIDE ON MERGER IN DEC.

text.p: Shareholders of the Polish Bank Wspolpracy Regionalnej SA (BWR) and the small Bank Secesyjny (BS) will decide in December whether to go ahead with a planned merger of the two banks, BWR's spokesman said on Friday.
Franciszek Palowski told Reuters that BWR had completed a two-year restructuring programme of Bank Secesyjny, in which it has 35 percent of votes.

"There were plans that after the restructuring programme there would be a merger of BWR and Secesyjny. After two years ...Secesyjny has been cured, its capital raised and it should finish this year with a substantial profit," Palowski said.
"The form of the merger will be submitted for approval by shareholders -- on December 10 of Bank Secesyjny and then, if they approve it, by BWR shareholders on December 23," he said.
Palowski also said BWR was considering a merger with the BWR-Realbank in which it has 51 percent of votes and which is also undergoing a restructuring programme.
"In 1994 we signed with the central bank an agreement on restructuring of that bank and the process is still under way," he said.
Among BWR's major shareholders are the CPN SA fuel distributor with a 16.2 percent stake, a biotechnology institute with 11.1 percent and Stalexport with 6.2 percent.

The net profit of BWR in the first 10 months of this year was 4.1 million zlotys against 2.4 million in the same period of 1995, on revenue from interest at 72.8 million against 43.2 million in the same period last year.
